newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 30.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
KATHIMERINI

--On the strike front, the only certainty is that schools are shut indefinitely and farmers have left the national roads open for the moment. It is within this context that the government is moving at the moment, calling on both sides to realise the need for (fruitless) dialogue.

--Despite recent warnings from Prime Minister Costas Simitis, squabbling between leading members of ruling party PASOK continues unabated. Education Minister and former defence minister Gerasimos Arsenis was targetted by Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos for his handling of the armed forces during the Imia crisis a year ago.
--The resolution of Greek-Turkish differences over the Aegean at the International Court at the Hague is the only way, British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said yesterday.
ELEFTHEROTYPIA

--Mutiny within the ranks of PASOK last night at Parliament during discussion of an amendment on benefits for large families. Some 30 PASOK MPs threatened to cross the floor to vote down the bill despite three changes by National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou. The session will continue today.
--Thessaly farmers have decided to cut the Athens-Thessaloniki rail link today, following last night's rowdy welcome for Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas in Thessaloniki.
--The recent upheavals in Greece's Balkan neighbours have left Greek firms with investments with a headache.

--Responses by Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis to questions on his plans for Greek universities have only served to further cloud the issue. Meanwhile, striking teachers yesterday marched through central Athens in support of their demands.
TA NEA

--The defence ministry is considering reducing the length of national service for those who choose to do their service at age 18. Other incentives are expected for graduates who enlist immediately after completing school. Alternative service is also being considered for conscientious objectors, but they will serve for twice as long.
--The head of Greece's athletics federation has threatened to call off the World Championships in Athletics slated for Athens later this year, in a dispute with Sports Undersecretary Andreas Fouras.
ETHNOS

--Following the discovery of a bomb at Athens' courthouses on Tuesday, more than 200 hoaxers called to warn of bombs at companies, courts and television and radio stations yesterday. Frantic police found nothing.
--Hands will go deep into pockets to pay new car insurance premiums this year as new rates submitted to the development ministry show increases of between 1.54 and 52.94 percent.
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS

--One of the robbers in a post office heist that netted 95 million drachmas on Monday may be a member of the notorious November 17 group. Reports say a police profile of the man is similar to descriptions of one involved in a bomb attack on police in 1992.
--A new study reveals that 17 percent of Greek girls and 7 percent of boys were sexually abused as children - the majority by family members.
--Andreas Papandreou's widow, Dimitra Liani, in the limelight again, this time accused of passing fake documents to the press.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
